links.outcome: Prediction stability and accuracy under answer-option shuffling, few-shot, CoT, and context truncation perturbations
links.effect: Shuffling options changed predictions 59.1% of the time, accuracy dropping up to 27.4 points; few-shot lowered performance 11.9% and raised position bias from 0.14 to 0.47; CoT lowered accuracy 5.7%.
links.quote: Shuffling answer options causes the model to change predictions 59.1% of the time, with accuracy dropping up to 27.4 percentage points.

unlisted_practices: Cloze log-probability scoring instead of generated-text answers
Permutation voting across answer orderings to recover accuracy
Back-truncation rather than front-truncation of context

screen.practice: prompt strategy selection and permutation voting
screen.reason: The paper evaluates prompt design practices (chain-of-thought vs direct answering, few-shot prompting, permutation voting, context truncation) on medical LLM accuracy and robustness using medical QA benchmarks.
